events.summary: The record is a genuine FHWA outbound link discovered on the County corridor page, not the County page itself. The former approval applied the County parent's text to this selected federal endpoint. The parent is already published with original maps and open-house boards. Current official FHWA navigation identifies a later project number and anticipated 2028 work; it does not establish that the old URL redirects to that resource or that its historical content is independently useful. A source-identity constraint therefore remains after bounded recovery. Return this row to pending review rather than inventing source identity, scope or a separate quality approval.

The601-page December2019 plan contains airport demand, facility requirements, alternatives, environmental and sustainability analysis, and phased capital implementation for the City-owned Sunport. Both mission gates and substantive document quality pass independently. Its printing original remains explicitly linked by the current City adopted Rank3 plan index as the2020 adopted plan. ABQInfo already presents that adopted plan through a Legistar attachment, so any later implementation should improve the existing family rather than create a second entry. The280024902-byte original exceeds the object ceiling; official reduced/summary endpoints exist, but a compliant equivalent smaller original was not established. Retain the original with explicit archive and family-delivery holds.

The actual150-word City article names local roadway/bicycle projects, so both mission gates pass. Its content is a mutable striping/design list with incomplete Central wording, mixed completed/prospective statements,30percent design milestones, a2026 expectation and a small2025 grant. It lacks design analysis, adopted decisions, documented outcomes or a coherent durable program record. Existing Hanover concept sheets and7Bar speed study supply more substantial family evidence; Unique list facts support targeted research but do not justify a limited-content exception or a separate public entry.

The actual109-word article describes6925linear feet of gravel-road paving and1760feet of Oakhill/Sharp repaving serving Sandia Knolls, naming Geer,Hobart,Gilbert,Jennifer and Olive roads. It identifies County design, a490000-dollar final construction cost and June2015 completion. It establishes no City expenditure, service obligation, adopted Albuquerque plan, or material connection to the Albuquerque transportation network. East Mountains County neighborhood paving is outside mission scope; County jurisdiction and broader metro context cannot substitute. Its thin construction summary also supplies no independent durable planning analysis.

The107-word selected article records a3250-square-foot half-court/activity addition and emergency generator/transfer switch, a design consultant, anticipated March2013 construction and a separate Completed label. It provides no selected-project funding decision, siting analysis, designed emergency-service coverage or City obligation. Fresh City evidence documents a different2018adult-daycare/respite project on the same property, with a City/County MOU and City project management; current cooling guidance lists the existing senior center but explicitly mixes City and non-City facilities. Neither proves a material Albuquerque component of this particular2013addition. The sparse construction blurb also fails standalone quality independently of project importance.

The 267-word article describes County voice/data connections among Animal Care, fire facilities, community centers and a school fitness center, with short construction costs and milestones. It does not establish public broadband access, City funding or decisions, City traffic control, intergovernmental service obligations or another material Albuquerque component. Streets with Albuquerque names and physical fiber infrastructure do not establish the required connection. Generic fiber explanation and operational installation metadata also provide insufficient standalone public-policy information.

The 211-word page has meaningful septic-conversion purpose and precise neighborhood boundaries, but almost all remaining information is conditional easement/funding language, estimates, designer and contact details. It simultaneously says construction awaits a Sandia Pueblo easement and remaining funds, lists no contractor and says Completed March 2017. A later official 2018 request seeks North Edith water/sewer infrastructure for the Albuquerque-Bernalillo County Water Utility Authority, confirming a real shared-utility subject but not this page's completion or final scope. This selected tracker lacks a final design, adopted decision, funding outcome or reconciled historical narrative; its public value belongs in better utility-program evidence rather than a separate entry.

The selected page gives two pipe lengths, a connection to an existing manhole, County District 1 bonds, costs, contractors and design/construction dates. It contains no service-area analysis, capacity, network diagram, adopted utility decision or explanation of the larger development/network purpose. Its limited unique alignment facts are component evidence for the already represented Chico corridor, not sufficient standalone planning or public-policy content. The selected page fails quality independently of the importance of sanitary sewer infrastructure.

The actual page identifies an unincorporated-neighborhood improvement area, four unspecified funding-dependent phases, and a downstream pond collecting runoff east of Second Street. It gives WSP as designer, State Capital Outlay as generic funding, anticipated Early 2025 start and TBD cost/completion. It does not establish a City drainage obligation, City upstream catchment, funding decision, adopted Albuquerque plan or material City service connection for this phase. Even apart from scope, no pond dimensions/capacity, design document, phasing explanation, funding amount or public-decision analysis establishes unique durable standalone value.

The recovered blogItem article contains only 15 words instructing readers to download MRCOG_BernCo_Pres2015_Handout.pdf. That exact official attachment URL is already the source link beside the published Bernalillo County Transportation Projects Update. The existing archive is a useful six-page April 2 2015 cross-project snapshot, freshly verified at 1160457 bytes and SHA256 d2ecd51ed4db125ff651c03ba629647f4c8de3510c7270f4ccc6c573193944d8. The selected HTML has no unique program narrative, policy facts or status beyond delivering that retained original.

The actual 134-word article establishes collaboration among the City, County, SWAN and West Central Community Development Group, but only promises generic programming, survey/geotechnical site analysis, conceptual design and budget sizing. It contains no resulting program, space allocation, site findings, adopted design or intergovernmental funding/governance terms. The remainder is bidding/construction metadata, cost and contacts. This is a genuine City-related project whose selected short page nevertheless lacks enough unique durable planning information for independent publication.

The selected page documents County acquisition and cleanup on Edith just north of Osuna, then County recreation/4H alternatives and community preferences. It identifies County Parks GO Bonds and potential NM Cooperative Extension operation, not a City decision, expenditure, service obligation or adopted Albuquerque-area implementation connection for this facility. The later national historic-trail plan identifies Sandia Ranch among multiple sites including Albuquerque sites, but that does not establish the old facility alternatives' City connection or adopted outcome. A useful County planning narrative and an Albuquerque-area address do not independently pass the material Albuquerque gate.

The 132-word page identifies up to30homes, a shared kitchen/bathroom building, six funding contributions including COA$75,000, and construction/design estimates and contacts. Those are useful historical capital-source facts, but it contains no housing policy, governance or operator agreement, siting rationale, adopted design, service model, program results or capital decision instrument. The project clearly matters to Albuquerque; this sparse contractor/status page does not independently explain that public subject well enough for an additional entry. Better official program/governance material should carry a future family treatment, with this budget breakdown retained as supporting evidence.
